- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast periods, especially after recent spikes; reduce initial forecast values by 2–5%.
- After a sharp price spike, model tends to overshoot and fail to correct downward; apply a “cool-down” adjustment by reducing forecast by 3–8% for the next 3–5 days.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias — over-predicts when prices are falling, under-predicts when rising; adjust forecast by subtracting 1–3% of the recent 7-day average if price is trending down.
- Forecast lags behind true price movements by 1–3 days; shift forecast 1–2 days forward for short-term (1–7 day) horizons.
- Model underestimates price drops in the final 5–10 days of the forecast window; add 1–3% to forecast for the last 5 days if recent price is falling.
- Avoid overfitting to recent high values; if last 5 days are above 70, reduce forecast by 2–4% for next 3 days to prevent over-optimism.
